entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7371"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 10</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Prov.10.1-Prov.10.32">Pr 10:1-32</reference>. Here begins the second part of the book, Pr 10:1-22:16, which, with the third, Pr 22:16-25:28, contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pr 10:<reference osisRef="1Cor.15.33">1-15:33</reference> are mostly antithetic; and those of Pr 16:1-22:16, synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing.</title> <div sID="gen11383" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7371"/><hi type="bold">1. wise [and] foolish--</hi>as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom.<div eID="gen11383" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11384" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">maketh ... father--</hi>or, "gladdens a father."<div eID="gen11384" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11385" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heaviness--</hi>or, "grief." <div eID="gen11385" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 10 Pr 10:1-32 . Here begins the second part of the book, Pr 10:1-22:16, which, with the third, Pr 22:16-25:28, contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pr 10: 1-15:33 are mostly antithetic; and those of Pr 16:1-22:16, synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing. 1. wise [and] foolish-- as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom. maketh ... father-- or, "gladdens a father." heaviness-- or, "grief."

navigation_sections.title: Pr 10:1-32 . Here begins the second part of the book, Pr 10:1-22:16, which, with the third, Pr 22:16-25:28, contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pr 10: 1-15:33 are mostly antithetic; and those of Pr 16:1-22:16, synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing.
